title: Reading a Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) Bill: Actual Charges, Installment and Monthly Variance
content:
# Actual Charges, Installment and Monthly Variance on Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans)

## The rule

Each budget bill on Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) compares the period's actual leveled charges with the installment. An excess of actual charges over the installment is booked as a variance debit, and an excess of the installment over actual charges is booked as a variance credit, in each case for the difference to the cent. The actual charges stay on the service account; only the installment, plus any charges not leveled, is billed as due, so a member who pays the installment is current. A period whose actual charges equal the installment books no variance. No interest is charged or paid on the deferred balance, the interest rate being 0.00 percent on every plan.

## What happens each month

| The period's actual leveled charges compared with the installment | Booked to the deferred balance | Effect on the deferred balance |
|---|---|---|
| Actual charges higher | A variance debit for the difference, to the cent | Rises (more is owed) |
| Installment higher | A variance credit for the difference, to the cent | Falls (more credit) |
| Equal | No variance | Unchanged |

Whatever the comparison shows, the amount billed as due is the installment together with any charges that are not leveled. Paying that amount keeps the member current.

## Hypothetical months

*Hypothetical figures on a plan with a $140.00 installment and no charges outside the leveled charges:*

| Month | Actual leveled charges | Variance booked | Billed as due |
|---|---|---|---|
| January | $212.37 | Variance debit of $72.37 | $140.00 |
| April | $96.15 | Variance credit of $43.85 | $140.00 |
| May | $140.00 | None | $140.00 |

In January the member who pays $140.00 is current, although the actual charges were $212.37; the $72.37 difference is carried in the deferred balance, not billed as past due. No interest accrues on it.

## Questions answered

**Does the member owe the difference when actual charges run higher than the installment?** The difference is booked to the deferred balance as a variance debit. It is not billed as due on that bill; only the installment, plus any charges not leveled, is billed as due.

**Is interest added to a deferred debit or paid on a deferred credit?** No. Interest on the deferred balance is 0.00 percent on every plan.

**What if a month's charges exactly match the installment?** No variance is booked for that period.
